flows.name: View landing page and get started
flows.goal: Understand what personal dashboards are for and start using TidyDash.

steps.userAction: The visitor opens the landing page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows what personal dashboards are for with examples of notes, counters, checklists and link lists, how to start by creating a dashboard and adding widgets, and options to sign up or sign in.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up or sign in to begin.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-up or sign-in form to begin.

flows.outcome: The visitor understands TidyDash and has a path to sign up or sign in; nothing is stored and refresh shows the same landing page.

flows.name: Sign up
flows.goal: Create a new account to own private dashboards.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty account credentials form with an option to submit.

steps.userAction: The visitor fills in the credentials and submits.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates the account, signs the member in and shows their dashboard list.

alternatives.condition: The email or password is missing or invalid.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The new member has no dashboards yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty dashboard list with an option to create a dashboard.

flows.outcome: A new account is created and the member is signed in; refresh still shows them signed in on their dashboard list.

flows.name: Sign in
flows.goal: Sign back in to access my dashboards.

steps.userAction: The returning member chooses to sign in.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty account credentials form with an option to submit.

steps.userAction: The member fills in the credentials and submits.
steps.websiteResponse: The website verifies the credentials and shows the member's dashboards with name and last-edited time.

alternatives.condition: The email or password is missing or invalid.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The member has no dashboards yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty dashboard list with an option to create a dashboard.

flows.outcome: The member is signed in and sees their dashboard list; refresh keeps them signed in.

flows.name: Sign out
flows.goal: End the session so my dashboards stay private.

steps.userAction: The member chooses to sign out.
steps.websiteResponse: The website ends the session and shows the public landing page with options to sign up or sign in.

flows.outcome: The member is signed out; refresh shows the public landing page and dashboards are no longer visible until sign in.

flows.name: View dashboard list
flows.goal: See all my dashboards and when each was last edited.

steps.userAction: The member opens the dashboard list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows every dashboard the member owns with its name and last-edited time, most recently edited first, with options to create, open, rename, duplicate or delete.

alternatives.condition: The member has no dashboards yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty list with an option to create a dashboard.

flows.outcome: No data changes; refresh still shows the same list of the member's dashboards ordered by last edited.

flows.name: Create dashboard
flows.goal: Start a new empty dashboard to fill with widgets.

steps.userAction: The member chooses Create from the dashboard list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates and saves an empty dashboard named Untitled dashboard with last-edited set to now and opens it in the editor ready for renaming and adding widgets.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the list as it was and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: A new dashboard named Untitled dashboard is saved and appears in the list; refresh still shows it and opening it shows an empty editor.

flows.name: Rename dashboard
flows.goal: Give a dashboard a meaningful name.

steps.userAction: The member chooses to rename a dashboard from the list or editor.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the current dashboard name ready to edit.

steps.userAction: The member edits the name and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website updates the name, sets last-edited to now with a saved indicator, and shows the new name in the list and editor.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the name as required and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed name and offers to retry.
The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.

flows.outcome: The dashboard's name is updated and its last-edited time is now; refresh shows the new name in the list and editor.

flows.name: Duplicate dashboard
flows.goal: Make a full copy of a dashboard with all its widgets.

steps.userAction: The member chooses Duplicate on a dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates a full copy named Copy of {name} with copies of all its widgets and contents, sets its last-edited to now, and shows it alongside the original in the list.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.
The website keeps the list as it was and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: A copy named Copy of {name} with copies of all widgets is saved; refresh shows both original and copy in the list.

flows.name: Delete dashboard
flows.goal: Permanently remove a dashboard I no longer need.

steps.userAction: The member opens the dashboard list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows all of the member's dashboards with name and last-edited time ordered most recently edited first.

steps.userAction: The member chooses Delete on a dashboard.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no dashboards yet and offers to create one.
The website deletes the dashboard with all its widgets and items and shows the dashboard list without it.
Nothing is deleted; the website shows the dashboard list as it was.
The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.

flows.outcome: The dashboard and all its widgets are permanently gone; refresh still shows the list without it.

flows.name: Open dashboard in editor
flows.goal: Open a dashboard to view and change its widgets with automatic saving.

steps.userAction: The member opens the dashboard list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows all of the member's dashboards with name and last-edited time ordered most recently edited first.

steps.userAction: The member opens a dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the editor with the dashboard name, all its widgets in order with titles, sizes and contents, and a saved indicator showing changes save automatically.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no dashboards yet and offers to create one.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard has no widgets yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the empty editor with the dashboard name, saved indicator and an offer to add a widget.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.

flows.outcome: No data changes by opening alone; refresh still shows the same dashboard with its saved widgets and a saved indicator.

flows.name: Add widget
flows.goal: Add a note, counter, checklist or link-list widget to a dashboard.
preconditions: A dashboard is open in the editor.

steps.userAction: The member chooses to add a widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the widget type choices note, counter, checklist and link list with a title field.

steps.userAction: The member picks a widget type, enters a title and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website appends the widget at the end in medium size with type defaults, updates last-edited to now and shows the widget ready to configure and use with a saved indicator.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the title field and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the entered values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The member cancels adding the widget.
alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing is saved; the website shows the editor as it was.

flows.outcome: A new widget of the chosen type is appended at the end in medium size with defaults and last-edited is now; refresh shows it in place.

flows.name: Rename, move and resize widget
flows.goal: Arrange widgets by renaming, reordering and resizing them.
preconditions: A dashboard with at least one widget is open.

steps.userAction: The member opens the dashboard editor.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the dashboard name with all its widgets in order with titles, sizes and contents and a saved indicator.

steps.userAction: The member edits a widget title and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new title, updates last-edited to now and shows the widget with the new title and a saved indicator.

steps.userAction: The member moves a widget earlier or later relative to other widgets.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new order, updates last-edited to now and shows the widget in its new place; move choices for unavailable directions are disabled.

steps.userAction: The member changes a widget size between small, medium and large.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new size, updates last-edited to now and shows the widget with the new size and a saved indicator.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the empty editor and offers to add a widget.
The website marks the title field and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the entered title and offers to retry.
The website marks the size choice and keeps the widget unchanged.
The website keeps the previous size and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The widget was removed in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the widget is gone and shows the remaining widgets.

flows.outcome: Widget title, order and size are updated and last-edited is now; refresh shows the widget in its new place with new title and size.

flows.name: Remove widget
flows.goal: Permanently remove a widget I no longer need.
preconditions: A dashboard with at least one widget is open.

steps.userAction: The member opens the dashboard editor.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the dashboard with its widgets in order.

steps.userAction: The member chooses Remove on a widget.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the empty editor and offers to add a widget.
The website deletes the widget with its items, updates last-edited to now and shows the remaining widgets in order.
Nothing is deleted; the website shows the dashboard as it was.
The website says the widget is gone and shows the dashboard with remaining widgets.

flows.outcome: The widget and its items are permanently gone and last-edited is now; refresh shows the dashboard without it.

flows.name: Use note widget
flows.goal: Keep plain text in a note widget.
preconditions: A dashboard with a note widget is open.

steps.userAction: The member opens a dashboard with a note widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the editor with the note widget and its saved text and a saved indicator.

steps.userAction: The member edits the note text.
steps.websiteResponse: The website autosaves the text immediately, updates last-edited to now and shows the updated text with a saved indicator.

alternatives.condition: The text is longer than 5000 characters.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the text and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed text and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The note widget or dashboard was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says it is gone and shows the dashboard list.

flows.outcome: Note text is saved and last-edited is now; refresh shows the same text in the note widget.

flows.name: Use counter widget
flows.goal: Track a count with a label using increase and decrease.
preconditions: A dashboard with a counter widget is open.

steps.userAction: The member opens a dashboard with a counter widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the editor with the counter widget label and value and a saved indicator.

steps.userAction: The member edits the counter label.
steps.websiteResponse: The website autosaves the label, updates last-edited to now and shows the updated label with a saved indicator.

steps.userAction: The member chooses increase or decrease on the counter.
steps.websiteResponse: The website changes the value by one, allows negative values, saves immediately, updates last-edited to now and shows the new number with a saved indicator.

alternatives.condition: The label is longer than 80 characters.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the label field and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed label and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The counter widget or dashboard was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says it is gone and shows the dashboard list.
The website keeps the previous value and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: Counter label and value are saved and last-edited is now; refresh shows the same label and value.

flows.name: Use checklist widget
flows.goal: Track to-dos by adding items and ticking them off.
preconditions: A dashboard with a checklist widget is open.

steps.userAction: The member opens a dashboard with a checklist widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the editor with the checklist widget and its items with ticked states and a saved indicator.

steps.userAction: The member enters item text and adds it to the checklist.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new unticked item, updates last-edited to now and shows it with the other items and a saved indicator.

steps.userAction: The member ticks or unticks a checklist item.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new ticked state immediately, updates last-edited to now and shows the updated tick.

alternatives.condition: The checklist has no items yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the checklist widget with no items and an offer to add one.
The website marks the item field and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed text and offers to retry.
The website says the item is gone and shows the remaining items.
The website keeps the previous tick state and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: Checklist items and their ticked states are saved and last-edited is now; refresh shows the same items with the same ticks.

flows.name: Use link list widget
flows.goal: Keep titles with web addresses and open them.
preconditions: A dashboard with a link list widget is open.

steps.userAction: The member views the link list widget in the open dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the widget title and all its saved link entries with their titles and addresses, with a saved indicator and last-edited time for the dashboard.

steps.userAction: The member enters a link title and web address and saves the new entry.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the entry, prepending https when the address starts without http(s), shows it with the other entries, and updates last-edited to now with a saved indicator.

steps.userAction: The member chooses a link entry to open.
steps.websiteResponse: The website opens its web address in a new tab and keeps the dashboard unchanged.

alternatives.condition: No link entries are saved in the widget yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the link list widget with no entries and invites adding the first title and web address.

alternatives.condition: The title is empty or the web address is missing or not a valid web address.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The chosen link entry was removed in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the link entry is gone and shows the remaining entries.

flows.outcome: Link entries are saved and last-edited is now; refresh shows the same entries and choosing one opens its address in a new tab.

fields.label: Email
fields.meaning: Account identifier used to sign in and own dashboards

fields.label: Password
fields.meaning: Secret that protects the member's dashboards

fields.label: Dashboard name
fields.meaning: How the member refers to the dashboard in the list and editor

fields.label: Widget title
fields.meaning: How the member refers to the widget inside the dashboard

fields.label: Widget type
fields.meaning: What kind of content the widget holds

fields.label: Widget size
fields.meaning: How large the widget appears relative to other widgets

fields.label: Note text
fields.meaning: Plain text kept in a note widget

fields.label: Checklist item text
fields.meaning: Text of a single to-do inside a checklist widget

fields.label: Link title
fields.meaning: How the member refers to a saved web address

fields.label: Link address
fields.meaning: Web address that opens in a new tab when chosen

steps.websiteResponse: The website asks to confirm the deletion and says what else will be removed with it.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website deletes the record and what belongs to it.
Nothing is deleted; the record stays as it was.

assumptions.text: Dashboards in the list are ordered most recently edited first.
Moving a widget beyond the start or end keeps it in place; move controls for unavailable directions are disabled.
